paper_title: Sol-Attn: Accelerating Video Generation Inference via On-the-Fly Attention Sparsification

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Diffusion transformers are essential for high-fidelity video generation, but long token sequences make attention a dominant inference bottleneck. Training-free dynamic sparse attention alleviates this bottleneck by computing only selected key-value blocks, yet existing methods struggle to sparsify attention both efficiently and accurately for two reasons: (1) Rigid, unpredictable, and costly routing: selecting a fixed fraction of top-ranked blocks by proxy score imposes fixed budgets, whereas retaining blocks to reach a target cumulative proxy probability mass yields dynamic but potentially imbalanced budgets; both incur non-negligible overhead from computing and materializing proxy scores. (2) Lossy keep-or-drop sparsification: unselected blocks are discarded entirely, degrading accuracy under aggressive sparsity. These limitations motivate cheaper dynamic-budget routing while limiting accuracy degradation. In this paper, we introduce training-free Sol-Attn (Sparsifying online attention), which unifies dynamic routing, sparse computation, and approximation correction in a single online-softmax pass, achieving a better accuracy-efficiency trade-off in sparse attention. The core of Sol-Attn is on-the-fly block thresholding with proxy-score reuse, which selects critical blocks by comparing block proxy scores against a threshold during online softmax. This design enables dynamic yet controllable block budgets without materializing the proxy map, while directly reusing the proxy scores of unselected blocks to approximate their contribution. Experiments across image and video generation tasks show that Sol-Attn advances the quality-efficiency frontier of training-free sparse attention, delivering 2.1 times and 2.3 times end-to-end speedups for video generation and editing, respectively, while preserving visual quality.

Sol-Attn: Accelerating Video Generation Inference via On-the-Fly Attention Sparsification 1. Introduction Diffusion transformers (DiTs) [1] have become the foundation of video generation [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. However, the pursuit of higher-resolution and longer-duration generation results in increasingly long token sequences, making the quadratic complexity of self-attention [7] dominant inference bottleneck. Training-free dynamic sparse attention is an attractive remedy because it can accelerate pretrained models without changing weights [8, 9, 10, 11]. Yet current block-sparse methods still rely heavily on offline routing from compressed attention-score proxies and keep-or-drop sparsification, which expose two sharp limitations. (L1) Block routing is rigid, hard to control, and costly. For each query block, top-𝑘 selects the 𝑘 key-value blocks with the highest proxy scores, thus enforcing uniform budget across query blocks; top-𝑝 retains blocks until their cumulative probability mass reaches 𝑝, risking severe budget imbalance when attention patterns are diffuse or sink-dominated. Both strategies materialize the proxy score map and routing indices in HBM before sparse attention begins, incurring non-negligible memory traffic at long sequence lengths. (L2) Keep-or-drop sparsification is lossy. Unselected blocks are discarded entirely, even when they carry non-negligible attention mass, degrading accuracy under aggressive sparsity. These limitations point to tension between routing efficiency and sparse-attention accuracy: Can we achieve cheaper dynamic-budget routing while limiting accuracy degradation? We propose Sol-Attn, training-free sparse attention that fuses threshold-based dynamic sparsification into online softmax and reuses proxy scores to approximate unselected blocks, all within single kernel, thereby achieving better accuracyefficiency trade-off. This design is realized through three steps: Query-dependent thresholding. We observe that attention scores in pretrained video models are often near-symmetric and normal-like, suggesting that block selection can be performed by threshold-based filtering. Based on this insight, we propose query-dependent threshold estimated from lightweight score statistics such as mean and standard deviation. This threshold selects blocks under dynamic yet controllable budget, without materializing the full proxy map. On-the-fly sparsification. During online softmax, each query block scans the pooled-key sequence tile by tile to produce proxy scores. These scores are compared on chip with the query-dependent threshold, and blocks above the threshold are immediately dispatched to nested sparse attention loop over the original key-value tiles. Since each score is consumed as it is generated, no full proxy score map or routing indices need to be stored in HBM. Proxy-score reuse. Instead of dropping proxy scores after routing, Sol-Attn keeps them in registers during online softmax and reuses the below-threshold scores to approximate unselected blocks. This recovers part of the contribution from dropped blocks and reduces approximation error relative to dense attention. The exact and approximate branches share the same online-softmax state, unifying routing, sparse computation, and correction in one streaming operator. Experiments across image generation, video generation, editing, and refinement show that Sol-Attn advances the quality efficiency frontier of training-free sparse attention while preserving generation quality. It delivers 2.13.0 end-to-end speedups across video tasks and reaches 5.1 when integrated with complementary optimizations in Sol-Engine. 2. Preliminaries Attention and Online Softmax. Experiments 4.1. Experimental Setup Models. We evaluate text-to-video generation with Wan2.1-14B [2], HunyuanVideo-13B [3], and LTX 2.3-22B [4, 5], spanning increasingly long spatiotemporal sequences. Video-to-video evaluation covers editing with Bernini-14B [16] and refinement with SANA-WM Refiner [17]. We also evaluate native 2K text-to-image generation with Ideogram 4 [18] to assess the effectiveness of Sol-Attn at moderate sequence lengths. Metrics. We measure task quality using VBench [19] for text-to-video generation, pose accuracy for SANA-WM refinement, Bernini-Bench [16] for Bernini editing, and Qwen-Image-Bench [20] for high-resolution text-to-image generation. Across tasks, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS quantify fidelity to dense attention outputs. Because theoretical FLOPs do not necessarily reflect practical efficiency, we report end-to-end wall-clock speedup relative to dense attention. Baselines. We use FlashAttention-3 (FA3) [21] as the dense attention baseline and compare with recent state-of-the-art training-free sparse attention methods: XAttention (XAttn) [10], Sparse-VideoGen2 (SVG2) [8], and Piecewise Sparse Attention (PISA) [11]. For XAttn and SVG2, we adapt their officially recommended configurations to models not covered by the original releases, such as LTX, and match sparsity across methods for fair comparison. Implementation Details. We implement Sol-Attn with custom GPU kernels and profile on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Exact attention uses fixed 6464 physical blocks. Since the routing and approximation chunk size 𝐶 affects efficiency but not the mathematical output, we do not treat it as an ablation variable. Following prior work, for Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo, Bernini, and Ideogram 4, we use dense attention during the first 20% of denoising steps and in the first layer as warm-up. For the two-stage LTX pipeline, stage-1 uses an 8-step LoRA with dense attention throughout, whereas stage-2 uses Sol-Attn for all steps without warm-up. The SANA-WM refiner likewise uses Sol-Attn throughout. 4.2. Kernel Efficiency Evaluation Kernel Efficiency Evaluation. Figure 5a reports the kernel-level speedup of Sol-Attn over FlashAttention-3 across different sequence lengths and sparsity levels. The speedup increases consistently with both sequence length and sparsity, reaching 5.41 at 128K tokens and 90% sparsity. This consistent scaling trend demonstrates that the efficiency advantage of Sol-Attn persists throughout the 16K128K sequence-length range. Efficient On-the-Fly Sparsification. Figures 5b and 5c isolate the two system costs of sparsification: selection latency and intermediate memory. Top-𝑘 and top-𝑝 materialize and globally traverse the proxy map, with top-𝑝 further requiring cumulative selection over sorted scores. Sol-Attn instead consumes each score on chip as it is produced, making routing 11.5 and 32.7 faster, respectively. Tile-local routing state also keeps Sol-Attn near dense attention in processor memory, whereas SVG2s routing structures and permutation buffers require about 8 more memory. The approximate correction in Sol-Attn introduces only minor kernel overhead. At the end-to-end level, Sol-Attn is faster because it computes only lightweight thresholds and hides routing overhead within the online softmax pipeline, whereas BSA materializes routing indices externally. Efficient Unified Execution Pipeline. To break down the latency of our unified kernel, we compare Sol-Attn against cuDNN BSA, the state-of-the-art block-sparse attention implementation on H100 GPUs, using identical block indices at 10%, 15%, and 20% exact density. Since Sol-Attn fuses routing and approximate correction into the online-softmax pipeline of sparse attention, its kernel performs more work than BSA. Nevertheless, Figure 10 shows only 9.4%, 3.9%, and 1.6% kernel-level overhead, respectively, confirming that approximate correction is lightweight. The comparison reverses end to end once BSAs separate routing stage is included: Sol-Attn is 6.2%, 6.2%, and 6.6% faster because only threshold computation remains outside its attention kernel, while the routing work is largely hidden by other operations in the online-softmax pipeline. Unified execution thus makes on-the-fly routing nearly free in the end-to-end pipeline. 5. Related Work Block Sparse Attention. Block sparse attention reduces quadratic attention cost by computing only selected key-value blocks. Early methods reduce this cost through structured layouts [27, 28, 29] or content-based grouping [30, 31]. More recent work learns block selection or combines compression, selection, and local attention within native sparse architecture [32, 33, 34]. In video generation, existing methods exploit the spatialtemporal redundancy of DiTs in two broad ways. One line of work constructs structured sparse masks from recurring spatial or temporal attention patterns [35, 36, 37, 38]; another derives content-adaptive sparse patterns at runtime from lightweight block-level proxy scores [8, 39, 40, 41], achieving more flexible block selection. Routing Strategies. Dynamic sparse attention hinges on selecting informative key-value blocks efficiently. The most direct strategies apply top-𝑘 or top-𝑝 to block-proxy scores. SpargeAttn augments top-𝑘 selection with confidence threshold and then applies an online-softmax-aware threshold to skip negligible updates [9]. SpargeAttn2 [42] takes the union of top-𝑘 and top-𝑝 masks to avoid their complementary failure modes [42], whereas Twilight [43] first forms conservative top-𝑘 candidate set and then prunes it with top-𝑝 [43]. Other methods redesign the importance measure or filtering primitive: XAttention scores blocks by antidiagonal sums [10], while VecAttention retains scores within fixed margin of the running row maximum and fuses the comparison into tiled score computation [44]. Related systems reduce the search cost through query-aware page selection [45], hierarchical pruning [46], context-dependent sparse patterns [47], or learned semantic hashing [48]. Sol-Attn instead computes query-dependent threshold for each proxy row and applies it to scores as they are generated, enabling routing to proceed online within the online-softmax pass. Sparse Attention with Correction. Correction-based methods approximate contributions omitted by the exact sparse branch. PISA applies block-wise Taylor expansion to unselected blocks and combines exact and approximate terms within the same softmax numerator and denominator [11]. SVG-EAR uses centroid-based linear compensation with error-aware routing [49], and BA-Att introduces covariance-compensated block approximation [50]. SLA assigns critical weights to sparse attention and marginal weights to linear attention [51]; SLA2 adds learned routing, weighted sparselinear composition, and quantization-aware training [52]. Existing corrections either follow sparse pattern constructed in separate routing stage or require model fine-tuning. Sol-Attn instead derives routing and correction from the same token-to-block score tile in single online-softmax pass. 9 Sol-Attn: Accelerating Video Generation Inference via On-the-Fly Attention Sparsification 6. Conclusion We presented Sol-Attn, training-free sparse attention that combines threshold routing and approximate correction in single online-softmax pass without materializing proxy map. More broadly, our study explores new form of sparse attention in which routing is no longer separate prerequisite and unselected blocks are approximated rather than discarded. This unified streaming design substantially narrows the accuracy gap between sparse and dense attention with little additional overhead, yielding favorable qualityefficiency trade-off across diverse visual-generation tasks. Limitations and Future Work. Despite these encouraging results, Sol-Attn remains limited in both its current implementation and application scope. The B200 kernel does not yet fully exploit Blackwells performance potential and currently supports only forward inference, while our evaluation is confined to bidirectional diffusion-based visual generation and does not cover autoregressive video generation. Future work will address these limitations through further kernel optimization, extension to autoregressive models, and trainable implementation with backward support. 10 Sol-Attn: Accelerating Video Generation Inference via On-the-Fly Attention Sparsification A.
